topic: MBA Reports: Porter's, SWOT & Financial Ratios

copy.instagram:
If you’re just dropping a SWOT table into your MBA report and calling it a day, you’re likely stuck in the 2:2 lane. Professors aren’t looking for you to list facts; they want to see how you connect the dots between internal data and the brutal reality of the market. 

Slide 1: The 2:2 Trap. Listing bullet points without cross-analyzing internal capabilities against external threats. It’s too surface-level.

Slide 2: The 1st Class Blueprint. This is where you shine. Integrate VRIO core competencies with PESTLE macro-risks. Back it up with cold, hard financial ratios like ROIC or EBITDA. 

Slide 3: The Secret Sauce. Don’t just suggest a strategy—provide a budgeted implementation roadmap. That’s what gets the top marks.

Save this for your next strategic management submission. Need a second pair of eyes on your framework? Hit the link in our bio.

Late-night MBA report panic? We’ve all been there, staring at a blank page trying to make sense of financial ratios and strategic frameworks. Most students fall into the trap of just listing facts—but your professors are looking for critical synthesis, not a summary.

Here’s the difference between a mid-range grade and a First Class result:

• The 2:2 Trap: Listing bullet points in a SWOT table without cross-analyzing internal capabilities against external threats.
• The 1st Class Blueprint: Integrating VRIO core competencies with PESTLE macro-risks, backed by solid financial analysis (ROIC, EBITDA) and a realistic, budgeted implementation roadmap.
